prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single universally “best” Miami company — the right contractor depends on your ZIP code, budget, roof type, insurance situation and how well the contractor meets hurricane-rated standards. Instead of one name, use the checklist and verification steps below to pick the best local roofer for a hurricane-rated replacement.

What to require for a hurricane-rated roof
- Miami‑Dade NOA (Notice of Acceptance) for the specific roofing system and materials — must cover HVHZ (High‑Velocity Hurricane Zone) when applicable.  
- Manufacturer certification (e.g., GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) for the installer.  
- FORTIFIED or similar windstorm-resistant installation options if you want elevated protection.  
- Written workmanship warranty and manufacturer product warranty spelled out in the contract.  
- Proper permits and code compliance; contractor should handle permitting.  
- Proof of insurance (general liability + workers’ comp) and a current Florida roofing/contractor license.

How to evaluate companies (quick checklist)
1. Verify Florida license at Florida DBPR (search contractor license).  
2. Ask for the company’s Miami‑Dade NOA references for the exact system they will install.  
3. Confirm manufacturer certification and ask to see the installer certificate.  
4. Request at least three written, itemized estimates.  
5. Check recent local references and photos of completed hurricane-rated projects.  
6. Read Google/Yelp/BBB reviews and check for unresolved complaints.  
7. Confirm they will obtain permits and provide a start/end timeline.  
8. Get proof of insurance and a written lien waiver policy.  
9. Ask about hurricane-specific details: roof-to-wall connections, secondary water barriers, deck attachment and shingle/fastener schedule.  
10. Don’t pay large upfront sums; use a phased payment schedule tied to milestones.

Important questions to ask contractors
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see the numbers?  
- Do you install roofs to Miami‑Dade HVHZ NOAs? Which NOA numbers apply to my system?  
- Are you a certified installer for (manufacturer)? Can you show the certification?  
- What wind rating will my roof have when finished? (e.g., 110–150+ mph per NOA)  
- What warranty do you provide (workmanship, duration, transferability)?  
- Will you handle permits and inspections?  
- Do you provide help with insurance claims? (get specifics)  
- Can I have three local references with similar hurricane-rated jobs?

Where to verify credentials and reviews
- Florida Department of Business & Professional Regulation (DBPR) license search.  
- Miami‑Dade County Product Control / Building Department for NOAs.  
- Manufacturer websites for lists of certified contractors.  
- Better Business Bureau, Google Reviews, local Facebook community groups, Nextdoor.

Typical costs / timeline (very rough)
- Cost depends on roof size, deck condition, materials, and fastening system. Hurricane-rated replacements often cost more than standard roofs because of enhanced underlayment, fasteners, and specified installation per NOA. Expect a higher-end premium compared with a basic shingle job. Get itemized bids to compare.

Next steps I can help with
- If you give your ZIP code, I can draft a tailored list of questions, an email/template to request bids, and a short checklist you can use when contractors visit.  
- Or I can provide an example contract addendum or inspection checklist for a Miami‑Dade NOA‑based install.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and whether you need help with insurance claims or want a sample contractor questionnaire — I’ll draft those for you.
